subject: Renewal triage & MAP: BrightPath capacity uplift + ROI benchmarks
messages:
From: Dana Miller <dana@brightpath.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightpath.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — usage spike and MAP request

Hi Aditya,

We're starting our renewal planning for BrightPath and wanted to surface some changes on our side before the formal renewal packet. Q2 saw a sustained increase in token consumption after the recommendation engine launch — attached is the token-by-day export for Q2 (BrightPath_usage_Q2_2026.csv).

High level:
- Baseline run-rate (Jul–Aug): ~120M tokens/month
- Post-launch (Aug): daily peaks up to 9M tokens/day, pushing projected monthly run-rate toward 210–230M if retention holds
- Latency has been fine for now but occasionally spikes during batch inference windows (we've included a short note in the CSV)

We want a mutual action plan (MAP) that does three things: map usage to a committed footprint for the next 12 months, outline pricing/discount tiers for committed volume, and include options for short-term burst headroom to avoid production slowdowns. Also need a quick ROI sketch for Dedicated vs hosted burst credits — our infra team will care about predictability and unit economics.

Can you send a MAP + ROI recap this week? We're aiming to finalize terms with procurement by the end of September.

Thanks,
Dana Miller
Head of Platform
BrightPath AI

Attachments: BrightPath_usage_Q2_2026.csv
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Dana Miller <dana@brightpath.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightpath.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 16:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — usage spike and MAP request

Dana — thanks for the data, very helpful. I pulled the CSV into our usage dashboard and started a quick impact sketch; I also attached a first-pass MAP (redwood_renewal_MAP_v2.pdf) with two capacity scenarios and a short ROI table for Dedicated vs hosted burst credits.

Quick call? I have availability tomorrow (Thu) 10–11am or Friday 2–4pm PT to walk the MAP with your infra/procurement folks. If neither works we'll do a brief async run-through and iterate.

High-level takeaways from our side (top-line):
- Current run-rate aligns with what you reported (~120M/mo) but projected steady-state after the engine is ~220M/mo under conservative retention assumptions.
- Break-even for Dedicated starts near ~18–24 months for a modest committed footprint; with a 12-month term plus 6-month price protection, unit economics look favorable if monthly tokens exceed ~180M.
- Short-term burst credit plus prefix caching can smooth spikes and reduce peak costs while you evaluate committed capacity.

I'll pull Laura and Monica into thread to confirm numbers and pricing options.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | (415) 555-0122

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Renewal planning — usage spike and MAP request

Laura / Monica — forwarding BrightPath's raw CSV and Dana's note. Quick internal triage below; can you confirm we can deliver the numbers and a pricing offer by EOD Friday? Procurement wants to lock terms by end of month.

Quoted from Dana:
> Q2 saw a sustained increase in token consumption after the recommendation engine launch... projected monthly run-rate toward 210–230M if retention holds

Internal assessment / proposed approach (draft):
- Recommended committed scenario A (conservative): 12-month term, committed 1.8B tokens (~150M/mo), 12% unit discount off hosted list, 2 months of burst credits (up to 50% above commit) included.
- Recommended committed scenario B (aggressive uplift): 12-month term, committed 2.4B tokens (~200M/mo), 18% unit discount, 3 months burst credits + reserved slot guarantee (priority routing during capacity pressure).
- Optional Dedicated trial: 3-month evaluation on 2x A100-equivalent GPUs with migration playbook and a migration credit to offset ramp costs. Include SLO guardrails (latency 95th <= 450ms). SLO report (slo_latency_report_q2.pdf) attached.

ROI sketch (very high level):
- Current hosted run-rate cost estimate: $X/month (from dashboard) at existing consumption
- Committed scenario B reduces unit cost ~18% and provides predictability; break-even for migration costs estimated <6 months if feature-retention holds. Exact numbers in MAP.

Requests:
1) Laura — sanity-check the SLO/latency commitment and the dedicated trial sizing (2 GPU vs 4 GPU ask).
2) Monica — price-confirm: can we commit to the 18% off list at the 2.4B level with the 3-month burst credits and reserved slot guarantee? Also confirm approval threshold for a pilot credit.

If you both sign off, I'll convert the MAP to v3, add the ROI sheet, and loop Dana/procurement with an ask for a quick call next week.

Thanks — Aditya
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal triage & MAP: BrightPath capacity uplift + ROI benchmarks

Dana — thanks again for the CSV and the details. Attached is the updated MAP (redwood_renewal_MAP_v3.pdf) plus a short ROI appendix and the SLO summary (slo_latency_report_q2.pdf). Key points below to make review quick for procurement:

Executive summary:
- Recommended contract: 12-month term, committed 2.4B tokens (avg ~200M/mo) with 3 months of burst credits (up to +50% of monthly commit) and a reserved slot guarantee during peak windows.
- Pricing: 18% unit discount vs hosted list for committed volume; committed pricing locked for 12 months + 6 months of price protection for any agreed uplift within that window.
- Dedicated trial option: 3-month trial on 2x A100-equivalent reserved GPUs (migration playbook included). We will credit migration fees up to $25k to de-risk.
- ROI snapshot: at projected run-rate (~220M/mo), committed scenario B reduces monthly spend by ~18% and yields estimated total saving of ~$310k over 12 months vs pure burst credits. Detailed line items in MAP appendix.

Operational guardrails and next steps:
1) We propose a 30-min handshake call next Tue (Sep 22) 10:00–10:30am PT to walk the MAP and confirm procurement asks. Please tell me if that works.
2) If you approve scenario B, we'll prepare a redline-ready Term Addendum and a DocuSign (link included) for signatures.
3) Tech: we'll run a short performance baseline in week 0 of the pilot and commit to a 95th percentile latency target <= 450ms; see attached SLO report for current observed numbers.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/tx/3a9b-renewal-BP-2026-034
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/98765
